resources.description: A textbook introducing wireless communication fundamentals and networks such as cellular and wireless LAN systems from a practical perspective, for students and engineers.

resources.title: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
resources.author: William Shakespeare
resources.description: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare is a comprehensive collection containing all of Shakespeare's plays and poems. This standard volume gathers the playwright's entire output, including histories, tragedies, and comedies that have shaped literature for centuries.

resources.title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
resources.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
resources.description: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde is a Gothic horror novella published in 1886. resources.title: A Room with a View

Back in England, Lucy becomes engaged to the sophisticated but pompous Cecil Vyse.

resources.title: Middlemarch

resources.title: Crime and Punishment
resources.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
resources.description: Crime and Punishment is a novel published in 1866. It follows Rodion Raskolnikov, an impoverished former law student in Saint Petersburg who plans to murder an unscrupulous pawnbroker. He convinces himself that certain crimes are justifiable if committed by "extraordinary" men pursuing higher goals.

resources.title: Jane Eyre: An Autobiography
resources.author: Charlotte Brontë
resources.description: Jane Eyre: An Autobiography is a novel published in 1847. It follows the life of Jane Eyre from her oppressed childhood through her education and into adulthood, where she becomes governess at Thornfield Hall and falls in love with the mysterious Mr. Rochester.

resources.title: Little Women
resources.author: Louisa May Alcott
resources.description: Little Women; Or, Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy is a coming-of-age novel published in 1868-1869. The story follows four sisters—Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy March—as they navigate the passage from childhood to womanhood in Civil War-era Massachusetts.

resources.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
resources.author: Oscar Wilde
resources.description: The Picture of Dorian Gray is a philosophical fiction and Gothic horror novel published in 1890. When a beautiful young man wishes that his portrait would age instead of himself, his desire becomes terrifyingly real.

resources.title: A Tale of Two Cities
resources.author: Charles Dickens
resources.description: A Tale of Two Cities is a historical novel published in 1859. Set in London and Paris during the tumultuous French Revolution, it follows Dr. Alexandre Manette after his mysterious 18-year imprisonment in the Bastille and his reunion with his daughter Lucie.

resources.title: The Great Gatsby
resources.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
resources.description: The Great Gatsby is a novel published in 1925. Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, it follows narrator Nick Carraway as he becomes drawn into the world of his mysterious neighbor, Jay Gatsby, a wealthy millionaire who throws extravagant parties.

resources.title: The Secret of Chimneys
resources.author: Agatha Christie
resources.description: The Secret of Chimneys is a suspenseful detective novel written in the early 20th century. resources.title: Metamorphosis

resources.description: Metamorphosis is a novella published in 1915. It tells the story of Gregor Samsa, a traveling salesman who wakes one morning to find himself inexplicably transformed into a monstrous insect.

resources.title: The Enchanted April
resources.author: Elizabeth Von Arnim

resources.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
resources.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
resources.description: The Yellow Wallpaper is a short story published in January 1892.

resources.title: Twenty Years After
resources.author: Alexandre Dumas, Auguste Maquet
resources.description: Twenty years after is a novel serialized from January to August 1845. D'Artagnan, still a lowly lieutenant after two decades, is summoned by the despised Cardinal Mazarin during France's brewing rebellion.

resources.title: War and Peace
resources.author: Leo Tolstoy
resources.description: War and Peace is a literary work published in 1869. Set during the Napoleonic Wars, it chronicles the French invasion of Russia through five interlocking narratives following different Russian aristocratic families.

resources.title: Cranford
resources.author: Elizabeth Cleghorn Gaskell
resources.description: Cranford is an episodic novel published in 1853. Set in a small English country town, the work affectionately portrays a society of elderly women navigating genteel poverty and rigid social codes in a world slowly changing around them.

resources.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, Complete
resources.author: Mark Twain
resources.description: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, Complete is a novel published in 1876 about a mischievous boy growing up along the Mississippi River in the 1830s-1840s. Tom Sawyer and his friend Huckleberry Finn navigate childhood adventures that take increasingly dangerous turns when they witness a murder in a graveyard.

resources.title: The Scarlet Letter
resources.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
resources.description: The Scarlet Letter is a historical novel published in 1850. Set in Puritan Massachusetts during the 1640s, it follows Hester Prynne, who bears a child out of wedlock and must wear a scarlet "A" as punishment for adultery.

resources.title: The Confessions of St. Augustine
resources.author: of Hippo Augustine
resources.description: The Confessions of St. Augustine is an autobiographical work written between AD 397 and 400. In thirteen books composed as prayers to God, Augustine recounts his turbulent journey from a sinful youth to Christian conversion.

resources.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
resources.author: L. Frank Baum
resources.description: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz is a children's novel written in 1900. When a cyclone sweeps young Dorothy and her dog Toto from Kansas to the magical Land of Oz, she discovers only one way home: she must destroy the Wicked Witch of the West.

resources.title: Great Expectations
resources.author: Charles Dickens
resources.description: Great Expectations is a novel first published serially from 1860 to 1861. The story follows Pip, a young orphan living with his sister and her blacksmith husband on England's coastal marshes.

resources.title: Grimms' Fairy Tales
resources.author: Jacob Grimm, Wilhelm Grimm
resources.description: Grimms' Fairy Tales is a German collection of fairy tales first published in 1812. Beginning with 86 stories and eventually expanding to 210 tales across seven editions, this seminal work transformed oral folklore into written literature.

resources.title: A Modest Proposal: For Preventing the Children of Poor People in Ireland, from Being a Burden on Their Parents or Country, and for Making Them Beneficial to the Publick
resources.author: Jonathan Swift
resources.description: A Modest Proposal is a satirical essay written and published in 1729. The work shockingly suggests that Ireland's poor could solve their economic troubles by selling their children as food to the wealthy.

resources.title: Sense and Sensibility
resources.author: Jane Austen
resources.description: Sense and Sensibility is a novel published in 1811. When the Dashwood sisters are forced from their family estate into reduced circumstances, they face romantic trials that test their contrasting natures. Sensible Elinor guards her feelings while passionate Marianne wears her heart openly.

resources.title: A Study in Scarlet
resources.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
resources.description: A Study in Scarlet is a detective novel published in 1887. This groundbreaking work introduces Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson as they investigate a mysterious murder in London.

resources.title: Leviathan
resources.author: Thomas Hobbes
resources.description: Leviathan is a philosophical treatise published in 1651. Written during the English Civil War, it explores the structure of society and legitimate government through social contract theory.

resources.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
resources.author: Mark Twain
resources.description: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn is a picaresque novel published in 1884-1885. Told in vernacular English, it follows young Huck Finn as he escapes his abusive father and flees down the Mississippi River with Jim, an enslaved man seeking freedom.

resources.title: Wuthering Heights
resources.author: Emily Brontë
resources.description: Wuthering Heights is a novel published in 1847. Set on the Yorkshire moors, it follows two landowning families and their turbulent relationships with Heathcliff, a mysterious foster son. Driven by obsessive love, possession, and revenge that spans generations, the story unfolds through dark passion and cruelty.

resources.title: Ulysses
resources.author: James Joyce
resources.description: Ulysses is a modernist novel published in 1922. It chronicles one day in Dublin—June 16, 1904—following three characters whose experiences mirror Homer's Odyssey. Leopold Bloom parallels Odysseus, his wife Molly echoes Penelope, and Stephen Dedalus reflects Telemachus.

resources.title: A Doll's House
resources.author: Henrik Ibsen
resources.description: "A Doll's House : a play by Henrik Ibsen" is a three-act play written in 1879. Set in a Norwegian town, it follows Nora Helmer, a married woman navigating life in a male-dominated society where opportunities for self-fulfillment are scarce.

resources.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
resources.author: Washington Irving
resources.description: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow is a short story written in 1820. Set in 1790 in a secluded glen near Tarrytown, it follows Ichabod Crane, a superstitious schoolmaster who competes with local rowdy Brom Bones for the affections of wealthy Katrina Van Tassel.

resources.title: The Importance of Being Earnest: A Trivial Comedy for Serious People
resources.author: Oscar Wilde
resources.description: The Importance of Being Earnest: A Trivial Comedy for Serious People is a play first performed in 1895. Two young gentlemen lead double lives, each pretending to be named Ernest to escape social duties and win the hearts of their beloveds.

resources.title: Treasure Island
resources.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
resources.description: Treasure Island is an adventure novel published in 1883. When young Jim Hawkins discovers a mysterious treasure map in a dead pirate's sea chest, he sets sail with a crew to find Captain Flint's legendary buried gold.

resources.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
resources.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
resources.description: The Hound of the Baskervilles is a crime novel serialized from 1901 to 1902. Sherlock Holmes and Watson investigate a centuries-old legend of a demonic hound haunting the Baskerville family on the desolate moors of Dartmoor.

resources.title: Anne of Green Gables
resources.author: L. M. Montgomery
resources.description: Anne of Green Gables is a novel published in 1908. When eleven-year-old orphan Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables farm by mistake, the Cuthbert siblings had requested a boy to help with farmwork. Imaginative, talkative, and eager to belong, Anne must prove herself worthy of staying.

resources.title: Second Treatise of Government
resources.author: John Locke
resources.description: Second Treatise of Government is a political philosophy work published in 1689. Writing anonymously during England's turbulent revolution, Locke outlines a radical vision of society founded on natural rights and government by consent rather than divine authority.

resources.title: The Brothers Karamazov
resources.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
resources.description: The Brothers Karamazov is a novel published between 1879 and 1880. Set in 19th-century Russia, this passionate philosophical work explores profound questions of God, free will, and morality.

resources.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
resources.author: Agatha Christie
resources.description: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd is a detective novel published in 1926. When wealthy Roger Ackroyd is found stabbed in his study, the recently retired Hercule Poirot is called to investigate. The victim had recently learned the identity of a blackmailer from his fiancée, a widow who poisoned her husband.

resources.title: The Call of Cthulhu
resources.author: H. P. Lovecraft
resources.description: The Call of Cthulhu is a cosmic horror short story written in 1926 and published in 1928. After inheriting his grand-uncle's mysterious notes, Francis Wayland Thurston pieces together a terrifying puzzle involving disturbing dreams, ancient cults, and a monstrous entity called Cthulhu.

resources.title: The Souls of Black Folk
resources.author: W. E. B. Du Bois
resources.description: The Souls of Black Folk is a collection of essays published in 1903. This groundbreaking work explores the African-American experience through personal observations and social analysis.

resources.title: Poirot Investigates
resources.author: Agatha Christie
resources.description: Poirot Investigates is a short story collection first published in 1924. The eleven tales follow the eccentric Belgian detective Hercule Poirot as he unravels mysteries driven by greed, jealousy, and revenge.

resources.title: The Murder on the Links
resources.author: Agatha Christie
resources.description: The Murder on the Links is a detective novel published in 1923. Hercule Poirot and Captain Hastings travel to northern France to meet a client, only to discover he's been murdered and buried beside a golf course.

resources.title: The Turn of the Screw
resources.author: Henry James
resources.description: The Turn of the Screw is a gothic horror novella published in 1898. A young governess arrives at a remote country estate to care for two children, only to become convinced that supernatural forces haunt the grounds.

resources.title: A Christmas Carol in Prose
resources.author: Charles Dickens
resources.description: A Christmas Carol in Prose; Being a Ghost Story of Christmas is a novella published in 1843. It tells the story of Ebenezer Scrooge, a greedy miser who despises Christmas.

resources.title: Thus Spake Zarathustra: A Book for All and None
resources.author: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche
resources.description: Thus Spake Zarathustra: A Book for All and None is a work of philosophical fiction published between 1883 and 1885. Through the voice of the ancient prophet Zarathustra, Nietzsche delivers discourses on subjects ranging from the mundane to the metaphysical.

resources.title: The Time Machine
resources.author: H. G. Wells
resources.description: The Time Machine is a science fiction novella published in 1895. A Victorian scientist known as the Time Traveller journeys to the year 802,701, where he discovers humanity has evolved into two distinct species: the childlike Eloi and the savage Morlocks.

resources.title: Beyond Good and Evil
resources.author: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche
resources.description: Beyond Good and Evil is a philosophical work published in 1886. Nietzsche launches a fierce attack on traditional philosophy, accusing past thinkers of disguising moral prejudices as objective truth.

resources.title: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano, Or Gustavus Vassa, The African: Written By Himself
resources.author: Olaudah Equiano
resources.description: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano, Or Gustavus Vassa, The African is an autobiography first published in 1789. Born in present-day Nigeria around 1745, Equiano recounts his kidnapping into slavery as a child and his journey across continents.

resources.title: The Man Who Was Thursday: A Nightmare
resources.author: G. K. Chesterton
resources.description: The Man Who Was Thursday: A Nightmare is a philosophical novel with elements of adventure and satire, written in the late 19th century. The story revolves around the enigmatic character Gabriel Syme, a police detective who infiltrates a group of anarchists in London to uncover their plans and identities.

resources.title: Peter Pan
resources.author: J. M. Barrie
resources.description: Peter Pan: [Peter and Wendy] is a work that began as a play in 1904 and became a novel in 1911. It tells the story of Peter Pan, a mischievous boy who can fly and never grows up. He whisks Wendy Darling and her brothers away to Neverland, a magical island inhabited by mermaids, fairies, and pirates.

resources.title: The Innocence of Father Brown
resources.author: G. K. Chesterton
resources.description: The Innocence of Father Brown is a collection of detective stories written in the early 20th century.

resources.title: On Liberty
resources.author: John Stuart Mill
resources.description: On Liberty is an essay published in 1859. Mill applies utilitarian ethics to explore the relationship between individual freedom and governmental authority. He warns against the "tyranny of the majority" in democracies and argues that personal liberty should only be restricted to prevent harm to others.

resources.title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
resources.author: Agatha Christie
resources.description: The Mysterious Affair at Styles is a detective novel written in the early 20th century. The story centers around the mysterious death of an elderly matriarch, Mrs. Inglethorp, at Styles Court, her estate in Essex, and the subsequent investigation into the incident.

resources.title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
resources.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
resources.description: The Return of Sherlock Holmes is a collection of 13 stories published in 1905. After Holmes's apparent death in 1893's "The Final Problem," Doyle faced intense pressure to revive his famous detective.

resources.title: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe — Volume 1
resources.author: Edgar Allan Poe
resources.description: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe — Volume 1 is a collection of various literary works, likely written in the mid-19th century.

resources.title: Emma
resources.author: Jane Austen
resources.description: Emma is a novel published in December 1815. Set in the village of Highbury, it follows Emma Woodhouse, a privileged young woman who fancies herself a matchmaker. Confident in her abilities, Emma meddles in the romantic lives of those around her, particularly her new friend Harriet Smith.

resources.title: The Phantom of the Opera
resources.author: Gaston Leroux
resources.description: The Phantom of the Opera is a Gothic horror novel first published in 1909-1910. Set beneath the grand Paris Opera House, the story follows a mysterious, disfigured figure known as the Phantom who haunts the theater's depths.

resources.title: The Cask of Amontillado
resources.author: Edgar Allan Poe
resources.description: The Cask of Amontillado is a short story first published in November 1846. Set during Carnival in an Italian city, it follows nobleman Montresor as he enacts revenge against fellow noble Fortunato for perceived insults and injuries.

resources.title: Autobiography of Andrew Carnegie
resources.author: Andrew Carnegie
resources.description: Autobiography of Andrew Carnegie is a historical account written in the early 20th century. This memoir provides insights into the life of Andrew Carnegie, detailing his humble beginnings in Scotland, his rise as a prominent industrialist in America, and his philanthropic efforts.

resources.title: Letters from a Self-Made Merchant to His Son
resources.author: George Horace Lorimer
resources.description: Letters from a Self-Made Merchant to His Son is a collection of letters written in the early 20th century. The correspondence is between John Graham, a successful merchant in the meatpacking industry, and his son, Pierrepont, who is attending Harvard University.

resources.title: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day
resources.author: Arnold Bennett
resources.description: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day is a self-help guide written in the early 20th century. This philosophical examination explores the concept of time management and emphasizes the significance of effectively utilizing the daily 24 hours we all possess.

resources.title: The Theory of the Leisure Class
resources.author: Thorstein Veblen
resources.description: The Theory of the Leisure Class is an economic and sociological work published in 1899. Veblen introduces the concept of conspicuous leisure—the practice of displaying wealth and status through visible idleness rather than productivity.

resources.title: How to Analyze People on Sight
resources.author: Elsie Lincoln Benedict, Ralph Paine Benedict
resources.description: How to Analyze People on Sight is a guide on human analysis written in the early 20th century.

resources.title: Tao Te Ching
resources.author: Laozi, James Legge
resources.description: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics is an ancient Chinese text from the late Warring States period (475–221 BCE). This foundational work of Taoism explores the Way and its Virtue through poetic wisdom.

resources.title: The Nicomachean Ethics of Aristotle
resources.author: Aristotle
resources.description: The Ethics of Aristotle is a foundational philosophical treatise written in the 4th century BC. This work serves as a comprehensive exploration of moral philosophy, addressing the nature of good character, virtue, and ultimately happiness, which Aristotle identifies as the chief aim of human action.

resources.title: On the Origin of Species
resources.author: Charles Darwin
resources.description: On the Origin of Species By Means of Natural Selection is a work of scientific literature published in 1859. It introduced the theory that populations evolve through natural selection, with life's diversity arising from common descent through a branching pattern of evolution.

resources.title: Common Sense
resources.author: Thomas Paine
resources.description: Common Sense is a pamphlet published in January 1776 advocating independence from Great Britain for the Thirteen Colonies. Written in clear, persuasive prose, Paine presents moral and political arguments to encourage common people to fight for egalitarian government.

resources.title: The Problems of Philosophy
resources.author: Bertrand Russell
resources.description: The Problems of Philosophy is a book published in 1912 that attempts to create a brief, accessible guide to philosophy's fundamental questions. Can we prove an external world exists? Can we validate cause and effect or justify morality?

resources.title: Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences
resources.author: René Descartes, John Veitch
resources.description: Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences is a philosophical and autobiographical treatise published in 1637. Descartes confronts skepticism by doubting everything to discover incontrovertible truth.

resources.title: Utopia
resources.author: Thomas More, Henry Morley
resources.description: Utopia is a work of fiction and socio-political satire written in Latin and published in 1516. This frame narrative depicts a fictional island society and its religious, social, and political customs.

resources.title: The Federalist Papers
resources.author: Alexander Hamilton, John Jay
resources.description: The Federalist Papers is a collection of 85 essays written between 1787-1788. Published under the pseudonym "Publius," these articles aimed to persuade New York voters to ratify the newly proposed Constitution.

resources.title: Essays: First Series (with Self-Reliance)
resources.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
resources.description: Essays — First Series is a collection of essays published in 1841 concerning transcendentalism.
